report_meta.report_title: Kestrel Citizen Portal Web Application Security Audit

introduction: This report presents the results of a grey-box security assessment of the Kestrel Citizen Portal, a fictional application used only as sample data.

engagement_scope.testing_type: Authenticated grey-box testing with two user roles

methodology.approach: Reconnaissance, automated scanning, manual verification and exploitation, reporting.

summary_table.title: Broken access control on token API
Stored cross-site scripting in feedback form
Missing rate limiting on OTP endpoint

detailed_observations.title: Broken access control on token API
detailed_observations.observation_description: PATCH requests to /v2/tokens/{id}/suspend and /v2/tokens/{id}/activate were accepted without an authentication header. Any network user could change the state of another user's token by supplying its numeric identifier.
detailed_observations.impact: An unauthenticated attacker can suspend or reactivate any citizen's access token, causing denial of service or restoring revoked access.
detailed_observations.recommendation: Enforce authentication and per-object authorisation on all token state transitions before release. Reject requests whose session does not own the token.
proof_of_concept_steps: Observe HTTP 200 and the token marked suspended.

detailed_observations.title: Stored cross-site scripting in feedback form
detailed_observations.observation_description: The feedback message field stored HTML unescaped and rendered it to administrators in the review dashboard. A payload in the message executed script in the administrator's session.
detailed_observations.impact: Script execution in an administrator session allows account takeover of privileged users.
detailed_observations.recommendation: Encode all user-supplied output contextually and apply a strict Content Security Policy on the admin dashboard.

detailed_observations.title: Outdated TLS configuration
detailed_observations.observation_description: The web tier negotiated TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 and offered CBC-mode cipher suites.
detailed_observations.impact: Legacy protocol versions expose sessions to known downgrade and padding-oracle attacks.
detailed_observations.recommendation: Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 and restrict cipher suites to AEAD ciphers.

detailed_observations.title: Missing rate limiting on OTP endpoint
detailed_observations.observation_description: The OTP verification endpoint accepted more than 500 attempts per minute for one mobile number without lockout or delay.
detailed_observations.impact: A six-digit OTP can be brute-forced within its validity window.
detailed_observations.recommendation: Limit OTP verification attempts per number and per IP, and invalidate the OTP after five failures.

detailed_observations.title: Verbose server banner
detailed_observations.observation_description: HTTP responses included a Server header disclosing the exact web server version.
detailed_observations.impact: Version disclosure helps attackers select known exploits.
detailed_observations.recommendation: Suppress or genericise the Server response header.

conclusion: Two high-severity issues were identified; the token API access control weakness remains open and should be fixed before the next release.
